description: Mercimek Corbasi is a beloved Turkish red lentil soup, known for its vibrant color, creamy texture, and comforting warmth. This simple yet flavorful dish is a staple in Turkish homes, perfect as a starter or a light meal. It's incredibly nourishing and easy to prepare, bringing authentic Turkish taste to your table.

instructions.title: Prepare Lentils and Aromatics
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. Drain well. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the vegetable oil and 1 tablespoon of butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Build the Flavor Base
instructions.text: Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, allowing it to deepen in color and flavor. Add the flour and cook for another minute, stirring to create a roux. This will help thicken the soup.

instructions.title: Combine and Simmer
instructions.text: Add the rinsed lentils to the pot, then pour in the chicken or vegetable broth (or water). Season with salt and black pepper. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender and have broken down.

instructions.title: Blend the Soup
instructions.text: Once the lentils are tender, remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, carefully blend the soup directly in the pot until it is smooth and creamy. Alternatively, transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender and blend until smooth. Be cautious when blending hot liquids.

instructions.title: Prepare the Chili Butter Sauce
instructions.text: While the soup is blending, prepare the finishing sauce. In a small pan, melt the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter over medium-low heat. Once the butter is melted and slightly foaming, add the dried mint and red pepper flakes (pul biber). Cook for about 30 seconds, stirring constantly, until fragrant. Be careful not to burn the spices.

instructions.title: Serve Mercimek Corbasi
instructions.text: Pour the hot soup into individual bowls. Drizzle each serving generously with the prepared chili butter sauce. Garnish with fresh chopped mint or parsley, if desired. Serve immediately with lemon wedges on the side for squeezing over the soup, which enhances the flavor beautifully.

tips: For extra creaminess and a slightly thicker texture, you can add a small diced potato or carrot to boil with the lentils and blend it all together.
Adjust the amount of pul biber (Turkish chili flakes) in the butter sauce to your spice preference; it adds a lovely warmth without being overly hot.
Always serve Mercimek Corbasi with a wedge of fresh lemon, as a squeeze of lemon juice brightens the flavors beautifully and is essential for an authentic taste.
article:
Discover the heartwarming embrace of Turkish cuisine through one of its most beloved and iconic dishes: Mercimek Corbasi, or Turkish Red Lentil Soup. This simple yet profoundly flavorful soup is a staple in Turkish homes and restaurants, cherished for its comforting warmth, nutritious profile, and incredibly satisfying taste. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a culinary novice, diving into the world of Turkish soups and stews offers a delightful journey, and Mercimek Corbasi is the perfect starting point. It's more than just a soup; it's a taste of Turkish hospitality, a bowl of liquid comfort that nourishes both body and soul.

## What is Mercimek Corbasi?

Mercimek Corbasi (pronounced mer-jee-MEK chor-ba-SUH) is a traditional Turkish soup made primarily from red lentils. It's renowned for its smooth, creamy texture and vibrant reddish-orange hue, often brightened further by a swirl of chili-infused butter and a squeeze of fresh lemon juice just before serving. This soup holds a special place in Turkish culture, often served as a hearty breakfast, a light lunch, or a comforting starter to any meal. Its simplicity belies a depth of flavor achieved through a careful balance of aromatics like onion and garlic, a hint of tomato paste, and a medley of spices, most notably dried mint and paprika. Mercimek Corbasi is celebrated not only for its deliciousness but also for its health benefits, being packed with protein, fiber, and essential nutrients from the humble red lentil. It's a testament to how basic ingredients can be transformed into something truly extraordinary and universally appealing.

## Ingredients for Turkish Red Lentil Soup

The beauty of Mercimek Corbasi lies in its simple, accessible ingredients, most of which you likely already have in your pantry. Using fresh, high-quality components will elevate the flavor profile significantly.

Here's what you'll need for an authentic Turkish Red Lentil Soup:

*   **Red Lentils:** Approximately 1 cup (200g). These break down beautifully, giving the soup its signature creamy texture. Ensure they are rinsed thoroughly.
*   **Onion:** 1 medium, finely chopped. Forms the aromatic base.
*   **Garlic:** 2-3 cloves, minced. Adds depth and a pungent warmth.
*   **Tomato Paste (Salça):** 1-2 tablespoons. Provides umami and a rich, slightly tangy flavor.
*   **Butter or Olive Oil:** 2-3 tablespoons for sautéing and for the topping. Butter is traditional for richness.
*   **Water or Vegetable Broth:** 6-8 cups (1.5-2 liters). Broth will add more flavor.
*   **Dried Mint (Nane):** 1-2 teaspoons, divided. A crucial spice that lends a distinct fresh aroma.
*   **Sweet Paprika (Tatlı Toz Biber):** 1 teaspoon. For color and mild flavor.
*   **Red Pepper Flakes (Pul Biber):** 1/2 - 1 teaspoon, or to taste. For a gentle kick, especially for the topping.
*   **Salt and Black Pepper:** To taste.
*   **Fresh Lemon:** Wedges for serving. Absolutely essential for balancing the flavors.

Optional additions can include a small carrot or potato, finely diced, to add extra body and nutrients, though traditionally, the soup is kept quite pure.

## How to Make Mercimek Corbasi: Step-by-Step Instructions

Making Mercimek Corbasi is a straightforward process that yields incredibly rewarding results. Follow these steps to create a bowl of authentic Turkish comfort:

**Step 1: Prepare the Lentils.**
Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes any starch and debris, ensuring a cleaner, better-tasting soup. Set aside.

**Step 2: Sauté the Aromatics.**
In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt 2 tablespoons of butter or heat olive oil over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and sauté for 5-7 minutes until it softens and becomes translucent. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.

**Step 3: Build the Flavor Base.**
Stir in the tomato paste, sweet paprika, and half of the dried mint. Cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, to toast the spices and deepen their flavors. This step is crucial for developing the rich base of the soup.

**Step 4: Add Lentils and Liquid.**
Add the rinsed red lentils to the pot. Pour in 6 cups of water or vegetable broth. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are completely soft and have started to break down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

**Step 5: Blend the Soup.**
Once the lentils are tender, remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, carefully blend the soup directly in the pot until it reaches a smooth, creamy consistency. If you don't have an immersion blender, transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender (be extremely cautious when blending hot liquids) and blend until smooth. Return the blended soup to the pot. If the soup is too thick, add more hot water or broth until you reach your desired consistency.

**Step 6: Prepare the Mint Butter Topping (Nane Yağı).**
In a small pan, melt 1 tablespoon of butter over medium-low heat. Once the butter is melted and slightly foamy, remove it from the heat and stir in the remaining dried mint and red pepper flakes. The heat from the butter will bloom the spices, releasing their aromatic oils.

**Step 7: Serve.**
Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into bowls. Drizzle each serving generously with the fragrant mint butter topping. Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges on the side. A squeeze of lemon juice just before eating is essential for an authentic Turkish experience.

## Pro Tips for the Best Mercimek Corbasi

Achieving that perfect, restaurant-quality Mercimek Corbasi is easier than you think with a few expert tips:

*   **Rinse Your Lentils Thoroughly:** This is non-negotiable. Rinsing removes excess starch, which can make the soup cloudy and sometimes bitter. Keep rinsing until the water runs clear.
*   **Don't Skimp on the Lemon:** Lemon juice is the secret ingredient that brightens and balances the rich flavors of the soup. Always serve with fresh lemon wedges and encourage a generous squeeze. The acidity cuts through the richness beautifully.
*   **Bloom Your Spices:** Sautéing the tomato paste, paprika, and dried mint briefly before adding the liquid deepens their flavor and aroma significantly. This "blooming" technique is a cornerstone of many Turkish dishes.
*   **Adjust Consistency to Your Liking:** Some prefer a very thick soup, while others like it thinner. Don't hesitate to add more hot water or broth after blending if the soup is too thick for your preference.
*   **The Power of Nane Yağı (Mint Butter):** The chili-infused mint butter topping isn't just for garnish; it adds a crucial layer of flavor and aroma that completes the soup. Don't skip this step!
*   **Taste and Adjust:** Always taste your soup before serving and adjust salt, pepper, or even a tiny pinch more dried mint if needed. Flavors can change as the soup simmers.

## Serving Suggestions & Pairings

Mercimek Corbasi is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in many ways throughout the day.

*   **Traditional Serving:** Serve piping hot, with a generous drizzle of the nane yağı (mint butter) and a fresh lemon wedge. The lemon is paramount for cutting through the richness and adding a tangy brightness.
*   **Bread is Essential:** Crusty Turkish bread, pita bread, or a simple slice of sourdough is perfect for dipping and soaking up every last drop of the delicious soup.
*   **Alongside Pickles:** A small dish of Turkish pickles (turşu) provides a wonderful tangy contrast to the creamy soup.
*   **As a Starter or Main:** In Turkey, it's common to have Mercimek Corbasi as a starter for a larger meal, but its hearty nature also makes it a satisfying light main course, especially when paired with bread and a simple salad.
*   **Complementary Salad:** A fresh shepherd's salad (çoban salatası) with finely chopped tomatoes, cucumbers, onions, and parsley, dressed simply with olive oil and lemon, makes an excellent accompaniment.
*   **Anytime Comfort:** This soup is particularly comforting on a cold day, when you're feeling under the weather, or simply when you crave a nourishing and satisfying meal.

## Variations and Dietary Adaptations

One of the great qualities of Mercimek Corbasi is its adaptability, making it suitable for various dietary needs and taste preferences.

*   **Vegetarian and Vegan:** This soup is naturally vegetarian. To make it completely vegan, simply use olive oil instead of butter for both sautéing and the topping. Vegetable broth can be used instead of water for extra flavor.
*   **Gluten-Free:** Mercimek Corbasi is inherently gluten-free, making it a safe and delicious option for those with gluten sensitivities. Just ensure any broth used is also gluten-free.
*   **Spice Level Adjustment:** The amount of red pepper flakes (pul biber) in the mint butter topping can be adjusted to your preference. Use less for a milder soup, or more if you enjoy a spicier kick.
*   **Add More Vegetables:** While traditionally simple, you can boost the nutritional content and texture by adding finely diced carrots, potatoes, or celery along with the onions and garlic. They will soften and blend seamlessly into the soup.
*   **Different Broths:** While water is commonly used, substituting vegetable or even chicken broth can add another layer of savory depth to your Mercimek Corbasi.
*   **Texture Variations:** If you prefer a slightly chunkier soup, you can blend only a portion of it, leaving some of the lentils intact for a more rustic texture.

Mercimek Corbasi is more than just a soup; it’s a culinary hug in a bowl, a testament to the power of simple ingredients transformed into something extraordinary. Its comforting warmth and rich, savory flavors make it a beloved dish across Turkey and increasingly, around the world. Whether you're seeking a nutritious meal, a comforting classic, or an introduction to the wonders of Turkish cuisine, this red lentil soup is an absolute must-try. Whip up a batch today and savor the authentic taste of Turkey!
